findings.issue: Gold overflow on add. saturating_add caps at u32::MAX (4.2B) not Gold::MAX (9,999,999). new_unchecked bypasses validation, so gold can silently exceed 9,999,999.
findings.notes: Confirmed by reading gold.rs:24. saturating_add(gain) where gain is unbounded u32.

findings.issue: Gold overflow on sell revenue. Same pattern as AUD-001: saturating_add can exceed 9,999,999.
findings.notes: Confirmed at shop.rs:272. total_revenue from saturating_mul is uncapped.

findings.issue: Gold overflow on UI sell path. player.gold.get() + price uses bare addition (not even saturating) — can panic on overflow AND exceed Gold::MAX.
findings.notes: Confirmed at shop_screen.rs:679. Bare + operator, not saturating_add. Worst of the three gold-add sites.

findings.issue: MineFloor wraps current_floor + 1 with new_unchecked. Game logic caps at floor 20 (line 56), so 21 is within MineFloor bounds (0..=120). Safe in practice but fragile — if cap changes to 120 later, floor 121 would violate bounds.
findings.notes: Game caps at 20, MineFloor allows 120. Safe now but coupling between game constant and type bound is implicit.

findings.notes: max_health is f32 in PlayerState (mod.rs:291), not a bounded type. Same pattern at combat.rs:304, interaction.rs:626/636.

proactive_analysis.finding: AUD-009: Zero validated new() calls across entire codebase
proactive_analysis.details: 336 total new_unchecked() calls. 0 new() calls. Bounded type validation only triggers during Serde deserialization (save/load). All runtime construction bypasses bounds entirely. Of 26 runtime-value new_unchecked sites, 3 are confirmed unsafe (AUD-001/002/003 Gold overflow), 6 are safe-by-clamping (.max(0.0), .min(max), saturating_sub with pre-check), 6 are safe-by-coincidence (Happiness u8 saturating ops can't exceed u8::MAX=255=Happiness::MAX), 5 are safe-by-current-constants (max_health=100.0 but not mechanically enforced), 3 are test helpers (safe), 3 are from trusted data sources (elevator_floors, clamped friendship, constant pool).
proactive_analysis.recommendation: Not an immediate bug — but the Builder should consider adding a helper method like Gold::saturating_add(self, amount) -> Gold that handles clamping internally, so callers don't need to remember .min(MAX). This is the bounded-type equivalent of the mechanical enforcement principle: make the wrong thing impossible to write.
